--- title: "[AalenAdditive]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Aalen additive hazards model with time-varying coefficients. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_aalen.py#L39-L501){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python AalenAdditive(*, nmin=None, test="aalen", qrtol=1e-07) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The additive hazards model is an alternative to Cox regression when the proportional hazards assumption fails. Instead of modeling the log-hazard ratio as constant over time, it models the hazard itself as a sum of covariate-specific, time-varying functions: $$ h(t \mid x) = \beta_0(t) + \sum_{j=1}^{p} \beta_j(t)\,x_j $$ Estimation proceeds by ordinary least squares at each event time: for each death, the coefficient increment $d\hat{B}(t)$ is obtained by regressing the event indicator on the at-risk covariate matrix. Cumulative coefficients $\hat{B}(t)$ are obtained by summing these increments. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nmin]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Minimum risk-set size. Event times where the risk set has fewer than `nmin` subjects are dropped (late-tail instability). Defaults to `3 * (p + 1)` where `p` is the number of covariates. [test]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["aalen"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Weighting scheme for the summary test statistics. `"aalen"` (default) uses equal weights, `"variance"` uses inverse-variance weights, and `"nrisk"` uses the number at risk. [qrtol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-07]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : QR decomposition tolerance for detecting rank deficiency (default `1e-7`). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit the Aalen additive model on the lung dataset: ::: {#495864f2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") aalen = gw.AalenAdditive().fit("Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex", data=lung) aalen ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` AalenAdditive (additive hazards, test='aalen') slope coef se(coef) z p Intercept 0.00483 0.005448 0.004703 1.158 0.247 age 8.986e-05 0.0001263 6.903e-05 1.829 0.0674 sex -0.003151 -0.003938 0.001222 -3.222 0.00127 n = 228, events = 165, event times used = 164 ``` ::: ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
cumulative_coefficients() Return the cumulative regression coefficients $\hat{B}(t)$ as a DataFrame.
fit() Fit the Aalen additive hazards model.
predict() Predict survival or cumulative hazard from the fitted Aalen additive model.
to_frame() Return the summary test table as a DataFrame.
### [cumulative_coefficients()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return the cumulative regression coefficients $\hat{B}(t)$ as a DataFrame. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_aalen.py#L453-L473){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python cumulative_coefficients(*, format=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each row corresponds to an event time. The cumulative coefficient for covariate $j$ at time $t$ is $\hat{B}_j(t) = \sum_{s \le t} d\hat{B}_j(s)$, the running total of OLS increments up to time $t$. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Columns: `time` and one column per term (Intercept plus covariates). ::: ### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the Aalen additive hazards model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_aalen.py#L127-L362){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit(surv, covariates=None, *, data=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} At each event time, an OLS regression of the event indicator on the at-risk design matrix produces one coefficient increment per covariate. The cumulative sum of these increments gives the cumulative regression function $\hat{B}(t)$. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv | Outcome | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A right-censored or counting-process `Surv` response. An `Outcome` or a formula string such as `'Surv(time, status == 2) ~ age + sex'` is also accepted, with its columns read from `data`. The right-hand side sets `covariates`. [covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A dataframe (pandas or polars), 2-D array, or formula string evaluated against `data`. A list of column names in `data` also works. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) holding the columns named by the response and `covariates`. When `surv` is an `Outcome` or a formula, rows with a missing value in any column used are dropped before fitting. Covariate formula strings and lists of column names are also resolved here. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [AalenAdditive]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The fitted estimator. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Fit the Aalen additive model on the `lung` dataset with two covariates. The summary shows the cumulative-regression test for each covariate: ::: {#90c8adae .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") aalen = gw.AalenAdditive().fit("Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex", data=lung) aalen ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` AalenAdditive (additive hazards, test='aalen') slope coef se(coef) z p Intercept 0.00483 0.005448 0.004703 1.158 0.247 age 8.986e-05 0.0001263 6.903e-05 1.829 0.0674 sex -0.003151 -0.003938 0.001222 -3.222 0.00127 n = 228, events = 165, event times used = 164 ``` ::: ::: The formula interface combines the response and covariates in a single string: ::: {#f3548bdb .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} aalen2 = gw.AalenAdditive().fit( "Surv(time, status == 2) ~ age + sex", data=lung ) aalen2 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` AalenAdditive (additive hazards, test='aalen') slope coef se(coef) z p Intercept 0.00483 0.005448 0.004703 1.158 0.247 age 8.986e-05 0.0001263 6.903e-05 1.829 0.0674 sex -0.003151 -0.003938 0.001222 -3.222 0.00127 n = 228, events = 165, event times used = 164 ``` ::: ::: ### [predict()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict survival or cumulative hazard from the fitted Aalen additive model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_aalen.py#L364-L451){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict(newdata=None, *, type="survival", times=None, format=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The cumulative hazard for a subject with covariates $x$ at time $t$ is $$ \hat{H}(t \mid x) = \hat{B}_0(t) + \sum_{j=1}^{p} \hat{B}_j(t)\,x_j $$ where $\hat{B}_j(t)$ are the estimated cumulative regression coefficients. Survival follows as $\hat{S}(t \mid x) = \exp(-\hat{H}(t \mid x))$. Because the additive hazard model can produce negative cumulative hazard increments for some covariate patterns, predicted cumulative hazards are clipped at zero. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [newdata]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Covariate values for prediction. A DataFrame, 2-D array, or `None`. When `None`, predictions are made for the training data subjects. A data frame may also hold other columns. The covariates are picked out by name and coded as they were at fit time, so the frame the model was fit on can be passed as is. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["survival"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Prediction type: `"survival"` (default) or `"cumhaz"`. [times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Query times at which to evaluate predictions. An array-like of positive floats. When `None`, the model's fitted event times are used. [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (auto-detect), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Columns `time` and `subject_1`, `subject_2`, etc., one row per query time. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#60266201 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") aalen = gw.AalenAdditive().fit("Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex", data=lung) aalen.predict(lung[:3], times=[180, 365], format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### [to_frame()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return the summary test table as a DataFrame. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_aalen.py#L475-L501){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python to_frame(*, format=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} One row per term with the slope (weighted average of increments), its standard error, z-statistic, and p-value. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Columns: `term`, `slope`, `coef`, `se`, `z`, `p`. :::
